```{r}
#| include: false
# library(): loads a package so its functions can be used in this session.
# normalizePath(): resolves a path into a canonical absolute path.
# getwd(): returns the current working-directory path.
# file.exists(): checks whether each specified file path exists.
# file.path(): joins path components with the platform-appropriate separator.
# dirname(): returns the directory portion of a file path.
# stopifnot(): stops execution if any supplied condition is FALSE; successful checks produce no output.
# read.csv(): reads a comma-separated file into a data frame; its first row supplies column names by default.
# read_data(): is a locally defined helper reading the specified course dataset; inspect its path and column mapping.
# c(): combines values into a vector, converting them to a common type when needed.
# factor(): stores categorical values; levels fixes their permitted order and labels can rename their display.
# unname(): removes names or dimension names without changing the underlying values.
# quantile(): computes sample percentiles; probs gives probabilities and type selects the interpolation rule.
# theme_set(): sets the default theme for subsequent ggplot charts in this R session.
# theme_minimal(): uses a minimal chart style; base_size controls the base text size in points.
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
project <- normalizePath(getwd())
while (!file.exists(file.path(project,"20261.Rproj")) && dirname(project)!=project) project <- dirname(project)
stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(project,"20261.Rproj")))
read_data <- function(name) read.csv(file.path(project,"data/module02",name))
audit <- read_data("audit_times.csv")$audit_days
restaurants <- read_data("restaurant_ratings.csv")
soft <- read_data("soft_drinks.csv")
e <- read_data("electronics_sales.csv")
quality <- c("Good","Very Good","Excellent")
restaurants$quality_rating <- factor(restaurants$quality_rating,levels=quality,ordered=TRUE)
q6 <- function(v,p) unname(quantile(v,p,type=6))
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size=14))
```

## 1. Variable meaning and tool selection

| Dataset and unit | Variable | Classification | Measurement level |
|---|---|---|---|
| Restaurant: one restaurant | Quality rating | Ordered categorical | Ordinal |
| Restaurant: one restaurant | Meal price | Numerical monetary measurement, recorded in whole USD | Ratio |
| Audit: one audit | Duration | Numerical elapsed-time measurement, recorded in whole days | Ratio |
| SoftDrink: one recorded purchase | Brand | Categorical | Nominal |
| Electronics: one week | Commercials | Numerical discrete count | Ratio |
| Electronics: one week | Sales | Numerical monetary measurement, recorded in hundreds of USD | Ratio |

Rounding or currency precision does not make a measured amount a count of entities. Accept a carefully justified distinction between an underlying measurement and its recording resolution. IDs and arbitrary category codes identify labels, so their arithmetic means lack the quantitative interpretation asked for here.

Use frequencies and bars for brand preference; distribution plots plus center/spread for Audit; group summaries/boxplots and conditional crosstabs for Restaurant; a scatterplot and suitable association measures for Electronics.

## 2. SoftDrink

```{r}
# table(): counts observations for each category or combination of categories.
# factor(): stores categorical values; levels fixes their permitted order and labels can rename their display.
# c(): combines values into a vector, converting them to a common type when needed.
# data.frame(): builds a table whose named columns have compatible lengths.
# names(): reads or assigns names to vector elements or table columns.
# as.integer(): converts to integers by truncating numeric fractional parts; it does not round to nearest.
# sum(): adds vector entries; on logical values it counts TRUE entries.
# kable(): formats a data frame or matrix as a readable report table; digits sets displayed precision.
# stopifnot(): stops execution if any supplied condition is FALSE; successful checks produce no output.
# all(): returns TRUE only when every supplied logical value is TRUE.
# ggplot(): starts a plot from data; additional layers are joined with +.
# aes(): maps variables to visual properties such as x, y, fill, color, or group.
# reorder(): orders factor levels by a summary of another variable.
# geom_col(): draws bars at supplied heights; it does not count records.
# labs(): sets axis titles, legend titles, plot titles, and captions.
f <- table(factor(soft$brand_book_label,levels=c("Coca-Cola","Diet Coke","Dr. Pepper","Pepsi","Sprite")))
s <- data.frame(Brand=names(f),Count=as.integer(f),Percent=100*as.integer(f)/sum(f))
kable(s)
stopifnot(all(s$Count==c(19,8,5,13,5)),sum(s$Count)==50,sum(s$Percent)==100)
ggplot(s,aes(reorder(Brand,-Count),Count))+geom_col(fill="#2878A5",width=.65)+
 labs(x="Brand",y="Recorded purchases",title="Coca-Cola is the most frequent recorded brand")
```

Coca-Cola accounts for **19/50 = 38%**. These are recorded purchases in a teaching dataset. Without a documented sampling design and target market, they do not establish population market shares or unique-person preferences.

## 3. Audit

```{r}
# q6(): is a locally defined helper computing type-6 sample quartiles for textbook consistency.
# c(): combines values into a vector, converting them to a common type when needed.
# kable(): formats a data frame or matrix as a readable report table; digits sets displayed precision.
# data.frame(): builds a table whose named columns have compatible lengths.
# length(): counts elements in a vector or list.
# mean(): computes an average; logical TRUE/FALSE values contribute 1/0, giving a proportion.
# median(): returns the middle sorted value, averaging the middle pair for even sample sizes.
# diff(): subtracts each preceding value from the next by default; diff(range(x)) gives max minus min.
# range(): returns the minimum and maximum as a two-element vector.
# sd(): computes sample standard deviation using denominator n-1.
# stopifnot(): stops execution if any supplied condition is FALSE; successful checks produce no output.
# all(): returns TRUE only when every supplied logical value is TRUE.
# ggplot(): starts a plot from data; additional layers are joined with +.
# aes(): maps variables to visual properties such as x, y, fill, color, or group.
# geom_histogram(): bins numeric observations; binwidth or breaks controls the intervals and boundary anchors them.
# labs(): sets axis titles, legend titles, plot titles, and captions.
# sort(): sorts values; decreasing=TRUE reverses the default ascending order.
# ave(): computes a grouped summary while retaining one result per original observation.
# geom_point(): draws a point for each row at its mapped x and y values.
# scale_y_continuous(): controls numeric y-axis breaks, labels, limits, and spacing.
q <- q6(audit,c(.25,.5,.75)); iqr <- q[3]-q[1]
lo <- q[1]-1.5*iqr; hi <- q[3]+1.5*iqr
kable(data.frame(Measure=c("n","Mean (days)","Median (days)","Range (days)","Sample SD (days)",
                           "Q1 (days)","Q3 (days)","IQR (days)","Lower fence (days)","Upper fence (days)"),
                 Value=c(length(audit),mean(audit),median(audit),diff(range(audit)),sd(audit),q[1],q[3],iqr,lo,hi)),digits=2)
flagged <- audit[audit<lo|audit>hi]
stopifnot(mean(audit)==19.25,median(audit)==18,all(q==c(15,18,22)),iqr==7,
          lo==4.5,hi==32.5,all(flagged==33),length(flagged)==1)
ggplot(data.frame(Days=audit),aes(Days))+
 geom_histogram(binwidth=5,boundary=10,closed="left",fill="#ACC9DA",colour="white")+
 labs(x="Audit duration (days)",y="Audits",title="Most audits finish below 25 days")
dots <- data.frame(Days=sort(audit));dots$Stack<-ave(dots$Days,dots$Days,FUN=seq_along)
ggplot(dots,aes(Days,Stack))+geom_point(size=3,colour="#2878A5")+
 scale_y_continuous(breaks=1:3)+labs(x="Audit duration (days)",y="Stacked observations")
```

The distribution extends farther toward long durations, with center around 18–19 days, a 12–33-day observed span, and a flagged 33-day value. Only 20 observations and a choice of bin width support a cautious description, not a stable estimate of the number of population modes.

Median **18 days** and IQR **7 days** are a reasonable typical-duration description in view of the long upper tail. Mean **19.25** and SD **5.44 days** add information about all observed magnitudes and workload variation. Accept another pair if justified and accompanied by its limitations. The 33-day value remains valid unless investigation supplies a reason to correct it.

## 4. Restaurant

```{r}
# split(): separates a vector or table into groups named by a grouping variable.
# do.call(): calls a function using a list of arguments, e.g. rbind to combine a list of tables.
# lapply(): applies a function separately to each element and returns a list.
# names(): reads or assigns names to vector elements or table columns.
# q6(): is a locally defined helper computing type-6 sample quartiles for textbook consistency.
# c(): combines values into a vector, converting them to a common type when needed.
# data.frame(): builds a table whose named columns have compatible lengths.
# length(): counts elements in a vector or list.
# min(): returns the smallest supplied value.
# max(): returns the largest supplied value.
# kable(): formats a data frame or matrix as a readable report table; digits sets displayed precision.
# stopifnot(): stops execution if any supplied condition is FALSE; successful checks produce no output.
# all(): returns TRUE only when every supplied logical value is TRUE.
# factor(): stores categorical values; levels fixes their permitted order and labels can rename their display.
# diff(): subtracts each preceding value from the next by default; diff(range(x)) gives max minus min.
# rep(): repeats values; times repeats a vector and each repeats individual elements.
# ggplot(): starts a plot from data; additional layers are joined with +.
# aes(): maps variables to visual properties such as x, y, fill, color, or group.
# geom_boxplot(): draws quartiles, whiskers, and flagged points; a flagged value is not automatically an error.
# geom_point(): draws a point for each row at its mapped x and y values.
# labs(): sets axis titles, legend titles, plot titles, and captions.
# cut(): groups numeric values into intervals; breaks sets edges and right=FALSE makes [left,right) intervals.
# table(): counts observations for each category or combination of categories.
# addmargins(): adds marginal totals to a table, normally row and column sums.
# rowSums(): sums each row separately.
groups <- split(restaurants$meal_price_usd,restaurants$quality_rating)
summaries <- do.call(rbind,lapply(names(groups),function(g){
 v<-groups[[g]];q<-q6(v,c(.25,.5,.75));d<-q[3]-q[1]
 inside<-v[v>=q[1]-1.5*d & v<=q[3]+1.5*d]
 data.frame(Quality=g,N=length(v),Median=q[2],IQR=d,Q1=q[1],Q3=q[3],ymin=min(inside),ymax=max(inside))
}))
kable(summaries[c("Quality","N","Median","IQR")],digits=2)
stopifnot(all(summaries$N==c(84,150,66)),all(summaries$Median==c(19.5,25,34.5)),
          all(summaries$IQR==c(10,12,11.5)))
summaries$Quality<-factor(summaries$Quality,levels=quality)
flagged_prices<-do.call(rbind,lapply(names(groups),function(g){
 v<-groups[[g]];q<-q6(v,c(.25,.75));d<-diff(q);o<-v[v<q[1]-1.5*d|v>q[2]+1.5*d]
 data.frame(Quality=rep(g,length(o)),Price=o)
}))
flagged_prices$Quality<-factor(flagged_prices$Quality,levels=quality)
ggplot(summaries,aes(Quality,ymin=ymin,lower=Q1,middle=Median,upper=Q3,ymax=ymax))+
 geom_boxplot(stat="identity",fill="#ACC9DA",width=.5)+
 geom_point(data=flagged_prices,aes(Quality,Price),inherit.aes=FALSE,colour="#B47816")+
 labs(x="Quality rating",y="Meal price (USD)",title="Prices differ in center, with overlapping distributions")
bands <- cut(restaurants$meal_price_usd,c(10,20,30,40,50),right=FALSE)
tab <- table(restaurants$quality_rating,bands)
kable(addmargins(tab))
high <- rowSums(tab[,3:4])
kable(data.frame(Quality=quality,Numerator=high,Denominator=rowSums(tab),Percent=100*high/rowSums(tab)),digits=2)
stopifnot(all(high==c(2,52,50)))
```

The >=30 shares are **2/84 = 2.38%**, **52/150 = 34.67%**, and **50/66 = 75.76%**. Boxplots preserve original numerical prices for center/spread comparisons; price bands show conditional proportions but discard within-band detail. Observational differences do not isolate effects of ratings. Possible confounding characteristics are not available in the file.

## 5. Electronics

```{r}
# kable(): formats a data frame or matrix as a readable report table; digits sets displayed precision.
# data.frame(): builds a table whose named columns have compatible lengths.
# c(): combines values into a vector, converting them to a common type when needed.
# cov(): computes sample covariance, with units equal to the product of the two measurement units.
# cor(): computes correlation; its default Pearson method measures linear association.
# stopifnot(): stops execution if any supplied condition is FALSE; successful checks produce no output.
# abs(): returns absolute values; a small tolerance in an equality check permits floating-point rounding.
# ggplot(): starts a plot from data; additional layers are joined with +.
# aes(): maps variables to visual properties such as x, y, fill, color, or group.
# geom_point(): draws a point for each row at its mapped x and y values.
# scale_x_continuous(): controls numeric x-axis breaks, labels, limits, and spacing.
# labs(): sets axis titles, legend titles, plot titles, and captions.
x<-e$commercials;y<-e$sales_hundreds_usd
kable(data.frame(Sales_unit=c("Hundreds of USD","USD"),
                 Covariance=c(cov(x,y),cov(x,100*y)),Correlation=c(cor(x,y),cor(x,100*y))),digits=5)
stopifnot(cov(x,y)==11,cov(x,100*y)==1100,abs(cor(x,y)-0.9304906)<1e-7,
          abs(cor(x,y)-cor(x,100*y))<1e-10)
ggplot(e,aes(commercials,sales_hundreds_usd))+geom_point(size=3,colour="#2878A5")+
 scale_x_continuous(breaks=1:5)+labs(x="Television commercials",y="Weekly sales (hundreds of USD)")
```

The ten weeks show strong positive, approximately linear association, with **r ≈ 0.9305**. Covariance is **11 commercials × hundreds of USD**, or **1100 commercials × USD** after conversion. Correlation stays unchanged under this positive rescaling. Neither a causal advertising effect nor stable future performance follows from these descriptions alone.

## Feedback priorities

Use the student checklist as the assessment criteria. Correct a wrong observational unit, denominator, sales unit, or causal interpretation before rewarding polished output. Accept statistically defensible alternatives to plot bins and summary recommendations when clearly explained. Refer to Lessons 2–4 answer guides for detailed working.
